messages.content: Let’s work on Washington for the school break. The dates are fixed: Thursday, October 10 through Monday, October 14. It’s Daniel, Owen, and me from Chicago. We’ll spend a lot of time at the Smithsonian museums, and we have dinner with family in Arlington Saturday night. Compare the airport and hotel-area combinations that make the trip easiest.

I’ll compare ORD flights into DCA and IAD, then pair them with areas that work for the museums and Arlington. Are you thinking four hotel nights with a Monday return, and do you have target arrival or departure windows?
Yes, four nights. We can leave Thursday after Owen gets out of school, so nothing before 4:30 p.m. Monday is still part of the break, and I don’t want to give away most of that day by leaving early.

That makes DCA materially stronger if the fares are reasonable. The workable nonstop is ORD-DCA at 5:35 p.m., arriving 8:28 p.m. The best IAD alternative leaves at 5:10 p.m. and arrives 8:04 p.m., but the longer transfer erases the earlier arrival. For Monday, DCA has a 6:45 p.m. nonstop arriving ORD at 8:03 p.m.; the comparable IAD flight leaves at 5:55 p.m. and arrives at 7:12 p.m.
What are the prices for all three of us, including one checked bag each way for the family, not three bags?

The DCA round trip is $1,146 for three tickets, plus $80 for one checked bag each direction, or $1,226 total. IAD is $942 for the tickets plus the same $80 bag cost, totaling $1,022. DCA costs $204 more before ground transportation.
Now pair those with hotel areas. I don’t need to be right next to every museum, but I don’t want a long commute twice a day either.

Three combinations are practical. DCA plus Penn Quarter gives the shortest museum days: about 15-20 minutes from the airport, then a 10-20 minute walk or short Metro ride to most Smithsonian stops. Arlington dinner is roughly 15-25 minutes by car. DCA plus L’Enfant Plaza is even closer to the National Mall and has direct Metro access to DCA, though the immediate area is quieter at night. IAD plus Rosslyn or Crystal City simplifies Arlington, but museum trips run about 20-35 minutes each way. Crystal City pairs better with DCA than IAD; from IAD it does not save enough to justify the airport transfer.
So IAD and staying downtown would be the cheapest flight but the most wasted time. Quantify that across the trip.

Correct. IAD to Penn Quarter is typically 45-65 minutes by car or about 60-75 minutes using rail and walking. DCA to Penn Quarter is usually 15-25 minutes. Across arrival and departure, IAD adds roughly 60-90 minutes. Its earlier Monday flight also costs about 50 minutes of usable sightseeing time. The likely total penalty is around two hours, possibly more if Thursday traffic is heavy.
And what do we gain or lose by staying in Crystal City with DCA? Saturday dinner is near Clarendon.

DCA plus Crystal City makes both airport transfers very short, generally 5-10 minutes, and Clarendon is about 15-20 minutes by car. The tradeoff is every museum day: allow 20-30 minutes each way by Metro and walking. Over three full sightseeing days, that can add roughly 90 minutes to two hours compared with Penn Quarter or L’Enfant Plaza. It may be worthwhile only if the room savings are substantial.
Give me the clean ranking. Cost matters, but preserving Thursday night and most of Monday matters too.

First: DCA plus Penn Quarter. It gives you the best balance of evening dining, museum access, a manageable Arlington trip, and nearly a full Monday. Second: DCA plus L’Enfant Plaza. It is strongest for Smithsonian access and airport simplicity, but has fewer convenient dinner options immediately around the hotel. Third: DCA plus Crystal City, worth considering if lodging saves at least about $250 total. Fourth: IAD plus downtown; it saves $204 on airfare but gives most of that value back in transfer cost and about two hours of trip time.

Use DCA and compare Penn Quarter against L’Enfant Plaza. Keep the 5:35 Thursday outbound and 6:45 Monday return. For the next pass, I want one room with two real beds, not a sofa bed, and the complete hotel total.

Understood. The focused comparison will use the DCA nonstop itinerary: Thursday ORD-DCA at 5:35 p.m., arriving 8:28 p.m., and Monday DCA-ORD at 6:45 p.m., arriving 8:03 p.m., currently $1,226 for three travelers with one checked bag each way. I’ll compare Penn Quarter and L’Enfant Plaza rooms that explicitly confirm two standard beds for all four nights, using totals that include taxes and mandatory fees. Nothing is booked yet.
